chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Muram and Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
the man performing Tamattu' Hajj, who enters [Mecca] on the night of Arafah, performs Tawaf and Sa'i, then releases from Ihram, then re-enters Ihram, and goes to Mina, he said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.وَيَسْعَى: And performs Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.يُحِلُّ: Releases from the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who performs Tawaf and Sa'i on the night of Arafah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the timing of the *Hajj al-Tamattu'* ritual, specifically permitting the release from Ihram (*Hul*) after Tawaf and Sa'i even if performed on the night of Arafah. It underscores the scholarly consensus that the strict separation of these rites from the day of Arafah is not a rigid condition, thereby facilitating pilgrims who arrive late or wish to optimize their schedule before proceeding to Mina.
